subject: Data transfer technical certainty, signing path, and subprocessor snapshot
messages:
From: procurement@healthmesh.com <Aisha Rahman>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: legal_ops@healthmesh.com <Tom Winters>, gcp-arch@healthmesh.com <Luis Ortega>
Date: 2026-10-18T09:12:00Z
Subject: Initial ask - DPA redlines + transfer assurances

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for running the quick call this morning. As we kick procurement for the pilot, HealthMesh needs the following items to complete our security and legal signoff: 

- A redline-friendly DPA (we received v2 but need to see your proposed changes clearly marked).
- Confirmation of whether Redwood will sign the UK IDTA / UK Addendum for our UK-hosted data and whether the signing path is DocuSign.
- A current subprocessor inventory with country of processing, purpose, and whether they hold keys (KMS/HSM).
- Technical note on onshore fallback and TIA/DTIA scope for our EU and UK tenants.

Can you get the DPA redline and the subprocessor CSV by EOD tomorrow? Also, our GCP architects asked for an explicit statement about KMS key jurisdiction for token encryption to satisfy our internal KMS policy.

Appreciate it — Aisha
Procurement Lead, HealthMesh

Hi Aisha — thanks, noted and happy to coordinate. Action plan below: 

1) DPA redline: I will send a redline PDF by tomorrow morning (we track changes on v3).
2) UK IDTA: We can sign the UK IDTA (Redwood legal has a standard UK Addendum). Kimberly is looped for confirmation on one narrow clause HealthMesh flagged in the call (related to onshore caching).
3) Subprocessor inventory: Laura will attach the CSV with processing country and KMS/HSM flag.
4) KMS jurisdiction: short answer — token encryption keys are in customer-configurable KMS regions; our default for EU tenants is EU-region KMS by default; I will include the operations note.
5) Signing path: DocuSign is preferred; can also route via your eSign tool if required (we use DocuSign account with legal@redwood.com).

I attached a quick timeline and the requested docs we have ready. If you need a legal call to walk through specific redlines, Kimberly is available tomorrow afternoon.

Next steps: I will send the redline and subprocessor CSV by 9:30am UTC on 2026-10-19.

Regards,
Stephanie Nguyen

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, procurement@healthmesh.com <Aisha Rahman>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-19T08:37:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial ask - DPA redlines + transfer assurances

Hi all — following up with legal guidance and what I will provide: 

- DPA redline (attached): We accepted most commercial edits and proposed narrow language for the onshore caching carveout to preserve availability. Please review section 6.2 (Processing Locations) and section 12 (Subprocessor Delegation).
- UK IDTA / Addendum: Redwood will execute the UK Addendum. Note: we do not sign third-party addenda that change our security obligations; we accept the UK IDTA as an addendum to our standard DPA with the mutually agreed TIA scope. I added a short comment in the redline around TIA sampling frequency.
- Subprocessor inventory: attached CSV includes processor name, primary processing country, purpose, and a KMS flag ("customer-managed-kms" or "redwood-managed-kms"). For clarity: subprocessors that perform model hosting (inference runtime) do not hold customer encryption keys; keys are in the KMS chosen by the tenant.
- KMS/HSM: We support both cloud KMS (GCP KMS / AWS KMS) and HSM-backed vaults for enterprise private deployments. Where customers require HSM, that is deployed in the region they designate; Redwood's control plane keys remain in Redwood legal's designated region for auditability.

I have attached three files: redline-dpa-v3.pdf (legal comments), subprocessor-inventory-20261018.csv, uk-idta-summary-compact.docx. Laura — ops note for fallback and TIA boundaries is below, please add if anything missing.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Stephanie / Kimberly / Laura — thanks for the fast turnaround and the files. Quick notes after review:

- We’ll circulate the redline to our counsel; the onshore caching language looks acceptable but our legal may request a small tweaks to the rollback clause — Tom (cc) will confirm by tomorrow.
- Subprocessor CSV: thanks, that meets our format. One ask — can you add an explicit column indicating whether the subprocessor's processing of HealthMesh customer data is transient (e.g., KV cache) versus persisted? That helps our procurement mapping.
- KMS note is very helpful. For our pilot we will request customer-managed KMS in the EU region. Please confirm the DocuSign envelope will be sent to legal_ops@healthmesh.com once we are aligned.

If we get procurement signoff tomorrow we expect to push the DocuSign envelope late Friday and hit a target go-live in three weeks. Appreciate your responsiveness.

Regards,
